Draft · independent audit in progress

Eight questions

How many members show up in the record?

Records involving Anthropic’s network name 452 of 533 serving members.

Serving-member join · Figure 01

The network includes Anthropic, its funders, funded groups, and their PACs and lobbyists. A lobbyist’s personal gift or outside spending against a member can put a dot on the chart.

Did Anthropic’s employees and PAC give to members’ committees?

What earns a dot

A member counts once if any of these kinds of public record names them.

Eight questions

Did Anthropic’s employees and PAC give to members’ committees?

Yes, and their gifts reached committees linked to 199 serving members by Sept. 30, 2026, up from 10 at the end of 2024.

FEC contributions to campaigns, leadership PACs and single-member joint fundraising committees

Employee gifts are personal money. PAC gifts come from Anthropic’s political action committee. Employment is as reported to the FEC, and amounts are before refunds.

Who did outside groups spend against?

Campaign gifts by serving member

Members are ranked by recorded employee dollars. A dash marks a source with no counted dollars.

Eight questions

Who did outside groups spend against?

74% of the outside spending shown went against Republicans, using money from all donors.

2016–2026 spending · members serving on Nov. 26, 2026
Each committee’s count starts at its first itemised network receipt on file.

Source · Federal Election Commission outside-spending filings

The filings identify the committee that spent the money. They cannot trace an expenditure to a donor or establish coordination with a candidate.

How big was the network in federal AI lobbying?

Largest totals by sitting member

All-donor spending by committees that received network money, counted from each committee’s first itemised network receipt on file. The lists follow the source figure’s rankings.

Eight questions

How big was the network in federal AI lobbying?

On 2025 filings naming AI, network clients reported 0.5% of the total, while frontier labs reported 6%.

Senate quarterly lobbying disclosures

Each amount covers all issues on a filing and gives an upper bound on AI lobbying. Outside-firm fees included in a client’s own reports count once.

Which bills came up most in reports filed for Anthropic?

The network’s share under two 2025 filing counts

The frontier-lab group comprises Meta, Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, OpenAI and xAI. Client matching and expense coverage are provisional.

Eight questions

Which bills came up most in reports filed for Anthropic?

Chip proposals led among individual bills named in the reports.

Federal lobbying reports and Congress.gov bill records

The counts cover bill mentions only. A mention leaves the company’s position open.

Did sponsors of the named bills get campaign gifts?

Leading bills in the filings

The ranking excludes broad legislative packages, including annual defence bills. A report can name more than one proposal. Titles are excerpts as introduced.

Eight questions

Did sponsors of the named bills get campaign gifts?

Serving sponsors of stand-alone bills in reports filed for Anthropic had campaign gifts on file more often than serving members overall.

Senate quarterly lobbying reports, Congress.gov bill records and FEC contribution filings

The records give no link between a gift and a bill.

Did House offices and political committees pay Anthropic?

Campaign gifts on file for serving sponsors

The chamber and timing comparisons use the reports filed for Anthropic. The last section adds other network clients.

Eight questions

Did House offices and political committees pay Anthropic?

Yes, and they paid OpenAI 2.3 times as much in the spending records collected here.

FEC committee spending reports and House disbursements · Figure 19

These payments were purchases, including Claude and ChatGPT. Committee coverage is partial, and card descriptions may bundle charges.
